check_busy.description: Busy check; reply[0] must be 0x31 before streaming.

check_device.description: Handshake probe; expects keyed 6-byte reply, key at reply[5].

get_device_name.description: Discovery/name query; reply[0] must equal the derived handshake key, name from reply[1].

set_ap_mode.description: Drop the device back to SoftAP/provisioning mode.

set_color.description: Set static RGB color (params occupy all three nonce slots).

set_device_name.description: Two-step rename: send this frame, await the 0x31 ACK, then send the new name as a raw UTF-8 payload.

set_ic_model.description: Set LED chipset model (WS2811, SK6812, etc. — index table not recovered).

set_pixel_count.description: Set pixel (dot) count; 2-byte big-endian hypothesis — confirm on hardware.

set_rgb_order.description: Set RGB byte order for the strip.

order.description: RGB order index (sync byte [5] reports current).

set_segment_count.description: Set segment count; 2-byte big-endian hypothesis — confirm on hardware.

sync_state.description: Fetch the 17-byte state block: [0]=0x38 [1]=device_on [2]=cur_mode [3]=cur_speed [4]=brightness [5]=rgb_order [6:7]=segment count (BE, clamped >=1) [8:9]=second count (BE; LEDs-per-segment vs secondary segment field — needs hardware capture) [10..12]=adapter RGB [13]=ic_model [14]=record/custom count [15]=white_brightness [16]=0x83.

toggle_power.description: Toggle power (the protocol has no discrete on/off). Read sync byte [1] first and only toggle when it disagrees with the desired state.

identity.notes: The protocol exposes no MAC/serial on the control channel, so the user-set device name (factory SSID-suffixed default, renameable via CMD_SET_DEVICE_NAME) is the only stable key the wire offers. A consumer may additionally pin the Wi-Fi MAC seen at join time.

methods.notes: Real discovery: TCP-scan the local /24 on port 8189. To each host that accepts, send a framed CMD_GET_DEVICE_NAME (0x77) and treat a reply whose first byte equals the derived handshake key as a found SP108E — the device name follows from reply byte 1. The keyed reply IS the identification: only a device speaking this protocol can answer it. While the device is unprovisioned it instead hosts an open SoftAP with SSID prefix SP108E_ at 192.168.4.1.

discovery.notes: No mDNS/SSDP/beacon. Discovery is active: TCP-scan the subnet on 8189 with a framed GET_DEVICE_NAME probe (see methods notes). Cheap pre-filter for a scanner: an open TCP listener on 8189.

device.manufacturer: SPLED-family (sold as SP108E by many resellers)
device.name: SP108E WiFi Pixel Controller (LED Shop)
device.notes:
The SP108E is a WiFi addressable-LED (SPI pixel) strip controller driven by the "LED Shop" Android app. It is Wi-Fi ONLY: the app declares no Bluetooth permissions and contains no BLE code. It is also FULLY LOCAL: the decompiled app contains zero http(s):// URLs — no cloud, no OTA, no analytics — so the INTERNET permission exists only for the raw sockets to the controller. A vendor shutdown can never brick this device; the rescue here is replacing the app, not the backend.
TRANSPORTS:
  * Control: TCP port 8189 (app socket layer: 1000 ms connect timeout,
    5000 ms read timeout, keepAlive on).
  * Provisioning: while the device hosts its SoftAP, the client binds local
    UDP 8188 and waits for the controller's broadcast token reply.
  * DISCREPANCY (document both): the prior public RE
    (blacklizard/LED-Shop-SP108E) drives the identical 0x38/0x83 framing
    over UDP 8189, successfully. App v1.13.0 uses TCP 8189 for all control
    traffic and UDP only in provisioning. The device most likely listens on
    8189 for both transports — the framing is transport-agnostic — but this
    needs a live unit to confirm. Clients should try TCP first and fall back
    to UDP.

FRAMING (HIGH confidence — decompile + blacklizard agree):
  Standard 6-byte command frame: [0x38, rnd0, rnd1, rnd2, CMD, 0x83].
  Bytes 1-3 are a per-frame random nonce chosen by the client; any nonce
  byte that would equal the START_FLAG (0x38) or END_FLAG (0x83) is
  incremented by 1 so it cannot collide with the flags. Up to 3 parameter
  bytes override rnd0..rnd2 in order — i.e. parameters are stuffed into the
  nonce slots, so no command carries more than 3 payload bytes. (Hypothesis:
  DOT_COUNT/SEC_COUNT params are 2-byte big-endian and fit because the nonce
  slots are free; confirm on hardware.)

HANDSHAKE KEY (HIGH): for CMD_CHECK_DEVICE (0xD5) and CMD_GET_DEVICE_NAME (0x77) the client derives a key byte from its three nonce bytes:
    key = ((b2 >> 5) & 7) | (b0 & 0x53) | ((b1 << 2) & 0xFD)
The device must echo the key in a fixed position: the discovery reply's first byte equals the key (the device name follows from byte 1); the AP-mode check reply is 6 bytes with the key at index 5. The nonce/key pair is a weak replay/rendezvous mechanism, validated by the device on handshake frames only.
ACK: most set-command replies are the single byte 0x31 ('1'). A wrong first byte means retry/fail.
SEQUENCING (from the app's command dispatcher): commands are serialized through a queue with a 200 ms inter-command delay under a lock. While the device reports "off", most commands are dropped — toggle, get/set name, sync, record-num, AP-mode and check-device are exempt. Preview/record streams retry once on a bad first reply. Set-name and set-password are TWO-STEP writes: send the framed command, await the 0x31 ACK, then send the raw UTF-8 payload.
CONFIDENCE SUMMARY: framing, nonce rule, handshake key derivation, ACK convention, ports (TCP 8189 / UDP 8188) and the full opcode map are HIGH (single decompiled source, corroborated on framing/opcodes by blacklizard). The 17-byte sync reply layout is HIGH as a decode map but its two segment-count fields need hardware to disambiguate (see sync_state notes). Custom-effect row streaming (preview/recode) is MEDIUM — the row byte layout was not fully traced. UDP-8189 acceptance is a hypothesis pending a live unit.

openness.notes: No vendor protocol documentation. This spec was recovered from the LED Shop v1.13.0 app; blacklizard/LED-Shop-SP108E is an independent open implementation of the same wire protocol (UDP variant) and serves as the cross-check.

credentials.notes: The passphrase crosses the wire under per-frame random-key XOR — keys transmitted alongside the ciphertext — which is obfuscation, not protection; marked plaintext in spirit. No credential is issued back to the client: control needs only LAN reachability, and the control port has no authentication.
stored_on_device: Optional device password (CMD_SET_DEVICE_PASSWORD; role in handshake untraced)

factory_reset.description:
Two published gestures that do not agree: a long hold of the controller's button, given as about thirty seconds, and a power-cycle-three-times sequence in some printed copies. Try the hold first.
One timing detail matters more than the reset itself. In station mode an unprovisioned controller waits only about twenty seconds after power-on for the app to hand it credentials, then stops listening. A user who resets it, goes to fetch their phone and comes back has already missed the window and has to power-cycle again.
factory_reset.effect: Restores factory settings and clears the stored WiFi credentials. Afterwards the controller hosts its own access point named SP108E_xxx with the default pin 12345678 — a product-wide default, printed in the vendor instructions.

procedures.basis: The SP108E operating instructions, as filed with the FCC under ID 2ATV8SP108E and reproduced by the vendor's distributors.
procedures.name: Hold the controller button for about thirty seconds

steps.action: With the controller powered, press and hold its button for about thirty seconds.
steps.expect: Factory settings are restored; the SP108E_xxx access point returns.

procedures.basis: An alternative given in some printed copies of the same instructions; recorded because the two disagree.
procedures.name: Power-cycle three times

steps.action: Switch the controller off and on three times.

methods.description: Client joins the device's SoftAP, hands it the home Wi-Fi credentials in a framed CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG over TCP 8189 (SSID/password/token XOR-obfuscated with per-frame random key bytes — obfuscation, not crypto), then confirms on the device's UDP 8188 token broadcast by sending CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG_OK. UDP 8188 is the token-reply socket named by the method type; the credential exchange itself is TCP 8189.

credential_encryption.algorithm: XOR obfuscation with per-frame random key bytes
algorithm_steps: Build the AP_NETWORK_CONFIG frame: [0x38, len_ssid, len_token, len_ipinfo, 0x26, 0x83, k0, (ssid XOR k0)..., k1, (token XOR k1)..., ipinfo...].
k0 and k1 are fresh random bytes chosen by the client per frame; each is transmitted in the clear immediately before the run it obfuscates.
Each SSID byte is XORed with k0; each token/password byte is XORed with k1. Decoding is the identical XOR.
This is wire obfuscation only — the keys travel with the ciphertext. Treat the passphrase as exposed to anyone watching the SoftAP segment.
credential_encryption.notes: Obfuscation-grade XOR, not encryption; there is no hardcoded key to recover because the key bytes are random per frame and sent alongside the data.

steps.action: Connect the phone/client to the device's SoftAP (SSID prefix SP108E_, open network).
Open a TCP connection to 192.168.4.1:8189 and bind a local UDP socket on port 8188 for the token reply.
Send framed CMD_CHECK_DEVICE (0xD5); expect the keyed 6-byte reply (key at reply[5]).
Send the CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG (0x26) frame carrying the XOR-obfuscated home SSID, password and a client-chosen token.
Wait on UDP 8188 for the controller's broadcast reply: starts with START_FLAG (0x38), bytes[2..5] = device IP, remainder = token text.
steps.expect: The token in the reply matches the token sent.

steps.action: On token match, send framed CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG_OK (0x27) over TCP 8189.
steps.expect: The device joins the home network and is thereafter found by the /24 TCP-8189 scan.

causes: Client socket not bound to UDP 8188 before sending the config frame.
Home network is 5 GHz — this class of controller is 2.4 GHz only.
Wrong passphrase; the device never leaves SoftAP mode.

setup.notes: Out of the box the controller hosts an open SoftAP (SSID prefix SP108E_, device at 192.168.4.1) and is driven directly from it — provisioning onto the home network is optional for control but is the normal flow. The whole flow below is recovered from the app's provisioning path and has NOT been replayed against hardware (hence medium, not high).

rejoin.notes: Two in-place paths: (1) while the device is on the old network, TCP-send CMD_SET_DEVICE_TO_AP_MODE (0x88), then re-run the SoftAP provisioning flow with the new credentials; (2) the normal provisioning flow itself whenever the device is reachable in AP mode. The old network must still be up for path (1) — if the router is already gone, power-cycle the device; controllers of this class fall back to SoftAP when their network disappears (unverified on this unit).

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Every fact comes from static analysis of LED Shop v1.13.0 (com.cdc.ledshop); the framing, opcode set and ports are corroborated by blacklizard/LED-Shop-SP108E, an independent Wireshark-based RE — with one transport discrepancy (UDP vs TCP 8189) documented below.

entities.name: LED Strip
entities.notes: State comes from sync_state (CMD_SYNC, 0x10): device_on at byte [1], mode [2], speed [3], brightness [4], white brightness [15]. Power is a TOGGLE on the wire: a consumer implementing turn_on/turn_off must read sync byte [1] first and send toggle_power only when it disagrees.

sp108e_protocol.discovery: TCP-scan the /24 on 8189; send framed CMD_GET_DEVICE_NAME (0x77); a reply whose first byte equals the derived key is a found device, name at reply[1..].

framing.ack: Single byte 0x31 ('1') acknowledges most set commands.
framing.command_frame: [0x38, b0, b1, b2, CMD, 0x83] — b0..b2 client-chosen random nonce; a nonce byte equal to 0x38 or 0x83 is incremented by 1; up to 3 parameter bytes override b0..b2 in order.
framing.handshake_key: key = ((b2 >> 5) & 7) | (b0 & 0x53) | ((b1 << 2) & 0xFD), computed from the three nonce bytes of CMD_CHECK_DEVICE / CMD_GET_DEVICE_NAME. Device echoes the key: discovery reply byte 0, AP-mode check reply byte 5.
framing.provisioning_frame: CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG: [0x38, len_ssid, len_token, len_ipinfo, 0x26, 0x83, k0, ssid^k0..., k1, token^k1..., ipinfo...] — XOR obfuscation with per-frame random key bytes k0/k1.
framing.provisioning_reply: UDP 8188 broadcast during provisioning: byte 0 = START_FLAG (0x38), bytes[2..5] = device IP, remainder = token text. On match the client TCP-sends CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG_OK (0x27).

opcodes.119: CMD_GET_DEVICE_NAME — discovery; reply = key byte + name from [1]
opcodes.136: CMD_SET_DEVICE_TO_AP_MODE — drop device back to SoftAP/provisioning
opcodes.16: CMD_SYNC — reply is the 17-byte state block (see sync_state)
opcodes.170: CMD_TOGGLE_LAMP — power toggle (no discrete on/off; read sync byte [1] first)
opcodes.20: CMD_SET_DEVICE_NAME — two-step: cmd frame -> 0x31 ACK -> raw UTF-8 payload
opcodes.213: CMD_CHECK_DEVICE — handshake; expects keyed 6-byte reply (key at [5])
opcodes.36: CMD_CUSTOM_PREVIEW — then stream rows, 0x31 ACK each (row format MEDIUM)
opcodes.39: CMD_AP_NETWORK_CONFIG_OK — sent after UDP 8188 token match
opcodes.47: CMD_CHECK_DEVICE_IS_COOL — busy check; reply[0] must be 0x31
opcodes.76: CMD_CUSTOM_RECODE — then stream <=300 rows, 0x31 ACK each (row format MEDIUM)

sp108e_protocol.sequencing: Serialize commands; 200 ms inter-command delay; drop non-exempt commands while device reports off (exempt: toggle, get/set name, sync, record-num, AP-mode, check-device); retry once on bad first reply for preview/record streams; set-name/set-password are two-step (framed cmd -> 0x31 ACK -> raw UTF-8 payload).
sp108e_protocol.transport: TCP, device listens on 8189 (SoftAP mode: 192.168.4.1:8189). Prior public RE (blacklizard/LED-Shop-SP108E) uses UDP 8189 with identical framing — device likely listens on both; TCP first, UDP fallback.
